## Takeaway #1: Start with self-service


Most support tickets aren’t complicated — they’re repetitive. A customer wants to know your return policy, hours, or order information. One of the clearest playbook takeaways is to give customers an agentic self-service experience: Instant answers, automated actions like starting a return, and smart escalation.


- **Start with your top questions:** Look at your last month of tickets and answer the ten questions that show up again and again.
- **Keep it searchable:** A help center only works if customers can find it — plain language beats clever category names.
- **Update it like a living document:** Add new answers as your product or policy changes, not once a year (or get an AI agent to do that).


## Takeaway #2: Let AI agents cover the gaps


Here’s the part that’s changed fastest:[Artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.salesforce.com/artificial-intelligence/) support tools used to mean clunky chatbots that frustrated customers more than they helped. That’s not the case anymore.


According to the playbook, 66% of service organizations report using[agentic AI](https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/what-is-agentic-ai/) today, up from just 39% a year earlier.[AI agents](https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/ai-agents/) can handle routine questions, escalate complex issues when needed, and provide around-the-clock support, freeing your team for the moments that need a human. For small teams, this matters more than it sounds like it should. Assistive AI can help your team with recommendations, tailored replies, and conversation summaries, so they make smarter decisions *faster* .


## Takeaway #3: Hyperfocus your channels


The third of these service playbook insights isn’t a tool at all — it’s discipline. Trying to keep customers happy across every platform spreads a small team too thin and invites long wait times. Instead, direct customers to the same few channels you can respond to frequently, and phase out the ones nobody’s using.


The playbook cites that 88% of customers say good service makes them more likely to buy again, and 72% say they’ll stay loyal to companies that respond faster. Being reliably fast on a few channels beats being spread thin across all of them. **What is small business customer service, exactly?**
It’s how a small or midsize business (SMB) handles support requests, questions, and complaints — everything from a help center to a live chat conversation. For lean teams, it usually means doing more with fewer dedicated support staff.


**Do I need AI tools to improve customer service for small business?**
No, but they help a lot. Self-service pages and clear processes go a long way on their own, and AI agents add speed and after-hours coverage once you’re ready to layer them in.


**How do I know which support channels to offer?**
Start with wherever your customers already are — email and phone are still common, but many small businesses are adding chat and social support based on customer habits. Track where requests come in and expand from there.


**What’s the biggest small business customer service mistake?**
Letting support and sales operate off separate systems. When teams can’t see the same customer history, service gets slower and customers feel it immediately. A connected[artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.salesforce.com/artificial-intelligence/what-is-ai/) and data setup fixes this at the root.
